content: Vonoprazan is a weak inhibitor of the CYP3A enzyme system. This characteristic necessitates caution when co-administering vonoprazan with drugs that are sensitive substrates of CYP3A, as it may alter their metabolism and pharmacokinetics. Below are detailed interactions and recommendations for specific drugs: 1. Alfentanil: Vonoprazan increases the plasma levels or effects of alfentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4-mediated hepatic and intestinal metabolism. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Amobarbital: Amobarbital decreases the plasma levels or effects of vonoprazan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. 3. Apalutamide: Apalutamide reduces the plasma levels or effects of vonoprazan through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 4. Armodafinil: Armodafinil decreases vonoprazan levels or effects by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute with an alternative therapy. 5. Atazanavir: Vonoprazan reduces the absorption and efficacy of atazanavir by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative. 6. Belzutifan: Belzutifan decreases vonoprazan levels or effects via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or substitute with an alternative therapy. 7. Carbamazepine: Vonoprazan increases carbamazepine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, carbamazepine reduces vonoprazan levels or effects through CYP3A4 induction. Close monitoring is required, and alternative therapies should be considered. 12. Carbonyl Iron: Vonoprazan reduces the absorption and efficacy of carbonyl iron by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Close monitoring is advised. 13. Cenobamate: Cenobamate decreases vonoprazan levels or effects via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or substitute with an alternative therapy. 14. Cilostazol: Vonoprazan increases cilostazol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Reduce the cilostazol dose to 50 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong or moderate CYP2C19 inhibitors. Close monitoring is recommended. 15. Citalopram: Vonoprazan increases citalopram levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16.
